nodes.description: In 53,030 UK Biobank participants with plasma proteomics, CH carriers had lower circulating FLT3 ligand and higher FLT3 receptor abundance, while the classical inflammatory cytokines IL6 and TNF were not altered after multiple-testing correction. This points to altered progenitor signalling rather than a systemic inflammatory cytokine signature. It is a cross-sectional correlate; whether it lies on the path to infection risk is untested.

evidence.snippet: In contrast, classical inflammatory cytokines including IL6 and TNF were not significantly altered after correction for multiple testing.

nodes.description: The mutant clone expands and contributes a growing share of blood cells. Clone size, measured as variant allele fraction (VAF), grades risk: clones with VAF above 0.4 substantially contribute to mature blood cells and carry the highest risks of malignancy and of serious bacterial infection. Splicing-factor clones (SRSF2) expand quickly and are often found large.

nodes.description: Clones carrying mutations in DNA-damage-response genes such as TP53, PPM1D and CHEK2 have a selection advantage under cytotoxic cancer therapy, and such clones precede therapy-related myeloid neoplasms.

evidence.reference_title: Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential and Clonal Cytopenias of Undetermined Significance: 2026 Update on Clinical Associations and Management Recommendations.
evidence.snippet: The clinical implications of CH are most relevant in therapy-related myeloid neoplasms (t-MN), with antecedent CH clones in genes such as TP53, PPM1D, and/or CHEK2 having a clear selection advantage.

nodes.description: CHIP is linked to a higher incidence and a worse prognosis of chronic heart failure. In mice, hematopoietic or myeloid Tet2 loss worsens cardiac remodelling through IL-1β and the NLRP3 inflammasome.

evidence.reference_title: Prognostic significance of somatic mutations in myeloid cells of men with chronic heart failure - interaction between loss of Y chromosome and clonal haematopoiesis.
evidence.snippet: Age-associated clonal haematopoiesis of indeterminate potential (CHIP) has been linked to increased incidence and worse prognosis of chronic heart failure (CHF).

nodes.description: Progression to myeloid malignancy, including myelodysplastic syndrome (see the Myelodysplastic_Syndrome entry) and acute myeloid leukemia. Clonal cytopenia without dysplasia (CCUS) sits between CH and MDS. Risk rises with clone size. Among carriers, a serious bacterial infection is followed by a higher risk of subsequent hematological malignancy, not explained by clone size alone.

nodes.description: CH carriers have a higher incidence of ischemic stroke. In a meta-analysis of 800,160 people across three cohorts, CHIP raised the risk of incident stroke (HR 1.20), for both ischemic (HR 1.18) and hemorrhagic (HR 1.25) stroke, and JAK2 and TET2 clones had the strongest gene-specific associations.

evidence.reference_title: Age-related clonal hematopoiesis associated with adverse outcomes.
evidence.snippet: The presence of a somatic mutation was associated with an increase in the risk of hematologic cancer (hazard ratio, 11.1; 95% confidence interval [CI], 3.9 to 32.6), an increase in all-cause mortality (hazard ratio, 1.4; 95% CI, 1.1 to 1.8), and increases in the risks of incident coronary heart disease (hazard ratio, 2.0; 95% CI, 1.2 to 3.4) and ischemic stroke (hazard ratio, 2.6; 95% CI, 1.4 to 4.8).

evidence.reference_title: Clonal Hematopoiesis and Risk of Stroke: Evidence From Over 800 000 Individuals Across 3 Cohorts.
evidence.snippet: This association was observed for ischemic (HR, 1.18) and hemorrhagic (HR, 1.25) stroke subtypes.

nodes.description: Loss-of-function TET2 mutation removes the enzyme's oxidation of 5-methylcytosine to 5-hydroxymethylcytosine in DNA, an epigenetic modification that influences gene transcription. In myeloid progeny of the clone this changes how macrophages respond to cholesterol.
nodes.id: Loss of TET2 Methylcytosine Dioxygenase Activity

evidence.reference_title: Clonal Hematopoiesis and Risk of Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease.
evidence.snippet: Tet2 catalyzes DNA hydroxymethylation22, an epigenetic modification that can influence gene transcription.

nodes.description: Not an approved CH therapy. In an exploratory substudy of the LoDoCo2 trial in chronic coronary disease, low-dose colchicine was associated with slower expansion of TET2-mutant clones than placebo. A cardiology review suggests that IL-1β inhibition and colchicine may benefit TET2 CHIP carriers in particular, but no prospective genotype-stratified trial has tested this.

evidence.reference_title: Colchicine and Longitudinal Dynamics of Clonal Hematopoiesis: An Exploratory Substudy of the LoDoCo2 Trial.
evidence.snippet: In this exploratory analysis, treatment with low-dose colchicine was associated with attenuated clonal expansion in TET2 CH.

evidence.reference_title: Clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential and cardiovascular disease: mechanistic insights, clinical implications, and the dawn of precision cardio-hematology.
evidence.snippet: The CANTOS trial exploratory analyses and subsequent studies suggest that IL-1β inhibition with canakinumab and colchicine may preferentially benefit TET2-mutant CHIP carriers, suggesting a future of mutation-guided cardiovascular prevention.

nodes.description: In cholesterol-loaded TET2-deficient macrophages, active JNK1 leads the deubiquitinase BRCC3 to deubiquitylate and activate NLRP3, so the inflammasome assembles and releases IL-1β. Isogenic human TET2-knockout macrophages derived from embryonic stem cells behave the same way. In mice, blocking BRCC3 reverses the accelerated atherosclerosis of Tet2 CH, and NLRP3 inhibition removes the worse cardiac remodelling of Tet2-deficient mice in heart failure models. The in vivo steps rest on mouse data.
nodes.id: NLRP3 Inflammasome Activation in TET2-Deficient Macrophages

evidence.reference_title: BRCC3-Mediated NLRP3 Deubiquitylation Promotes Inflammasome Activation and Atherosclerosis in Tet2 Clonal Hematopoiesis.
evidence.snippet: Increased JNK1 signaling led to NLRP3 deubiquitylation and activation by the deubiquitinase BRCC3 (BRCA1/BRCA2-containing complex subunit 3).

evidence.reference_title: BRCC3-Mediated NLRP3 Deubiquitylation Promotes Inflammasome Activation and Atherosclerosis in Tet2 Clonal Hematopoiesis.
evidence.snippet: Human TET2-/- macrophages displayed increased JNK1 and NLRP3 inflammasome activation, especially after cholesterol loading, with reversal by holomycin treatment, indicating human relevance.

nodes.description: Incident sepsis or bacterial pneumonia. In 590,537 individuals without a diagnosed hematological malignancy, CH was associated with serious bacterial infection (HR 1.22) and with 28-day post-infection mortality (RR 1.84). Risk is graded by gene and clone size: within 10 years, about 25% of people with a large SRSF2 P95 clone, 23% with a large IDH2 R140 clone, 18% with a large SF3B1 K700 clone and 9% with a large DNMT3A R882 clone developed an infection. The association held after adjustment for inflammatory comorbidities and ancestry, after excluding people with cytopenias, and in a cancer-free subset. It was largely independent of the causative bacterium. CH was not associated with viral infection.

nodes.description: In mice, Tet2-deficient macrophages exposed to low-density lipoprotein up-regulate chemokine (Cxcl1, Cxcl2, Cxcl3, Pf4) and pro-inflammatory cytokine (Il1b, Il6) genes, and hematopoietic Tet2 loss enlarges atherosclerotic lesions. This is the proposed route from TET2-mutant CH to coronary heart disease; the human association is established, while the macrophage mechanism rests on mouse data.

evidence.snippet: Cxcl1, Cxcl2, Cxcl3, Pf4, Il1b, and Il6 transcript levels were among the most highly induced in Tet2−/− macrophages in this set (Figure S7A–B).

nodes.description: Smoking is associated with CHIP in a UK Biobank analysis of about 460,000 participants, alongside age and several prior diseases. Whether smoking raises the somatic mutation rate or favours the growth of mutant clones is not established, so the link below records an association.

evidence.reference_title: Risk factors of clonal hematopoiesis of indeterminate potential.
evidence.snippet: We found that advanced age, smoking, history of several diseases (including breast cancer and leiomyoma of uterus), as well as several serum biomarkers (monocyte count, proteins LY75, SIGLEC6, SIRPB1 and CYB5R2) were associated with CHIP.
